title: Trigonometric Functions
summary: Radian measure, trigonometric functions of any angle, and their graphs.

topics.title: Angles and radian measure
topics.notes:
One **radian** is the angle subtended at the centre by an arc equal in length to the radius.

$$\pi \text{ radians} = 180^\circ \qquad 1 \text{ rad} \approx 57^\circ 16'$$

- Degrees to radians: multiply by $\dfrac{\pi}{180}$.
- Radians to degrees: multiply by $\dfrac{180}{\pi}$.
- Arc length: $l = r\theta$ (with $\theta$ in radians).

On the unit circle, the point at angle $x$ is $(\cos x, \sin x)$, so $\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$.

| | $0$ | $\frac{\pi}{6}$ | $\frac{\pi}{4}$ | $\frac{\pi}{3}$ | $\frac{\pi}{2}$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| $\sin$ | $0$ | $\frac12$ | $\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ | $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ | $1$ |
| $\cos$ | $1$ | $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$ | $\frac{1}{\sqrt2}$ | $\frac12$ | $0$ |

topics.title: Graphs and transformations
topics.notes:
$\sin x$ and $\cos x$ have period $2\pi$ and range $[-1, 1]$. $\tan x$ has period $\pi$ and is undefined at odd multiples of $\frac{\pi}{2}$.

For $y = a\sin(bx + c)$:
- **amplitude** $|a|$ stretches the graph vertically,
- **period** $\dfrac{2\pi}{|b|}$ squeezes it horizontally,
- **phase shift** $-\dfrac{c}{b}$ slides it left or right.

**Sum and difference formulas**
$$\sin(x \pm y) = \sin x\cos y \pm \cos x\sin y \qquad \cos(x \pm y) = \cos x\cos y \mp \sin x\sin y$$

Drag the sliders $a$, $b$ and $c$ in the graphing calculator to see each effect.

examples.problem: Find the period and amplitude of $y = 3\cos 4x$.

quiz.hint: Amplitude is the size of the coefficient in front of sin, so ignore its sign.
